# Fixes to the Chinese ROM

<!-- Generated by `python3 work/tools/fixes.py docs --out work/patches/FIXES.md` from work/patches/*/fix.toml. Do not edit by hand. -->

Besides the message text (`a/0/2/7`, `battle_string.narc`), the English build changes the untouched Chinese ROM (`origin_v4.0.3_cn.nds`) only through the fixes below. Each one lives in `work/patches/<id>/fix.toml`; a code, data or strings fix also has an armips source (`<id>.asm`, shown under the fix) that writes the new bytes, while fix.toml declares the regions it may change, their original bytes, the strings' Chinese and English and how far an overlay may grow, and the build refuses any other change (`work/notes/toolchain.md`). Each fix checks what it replaces before it writes: code, data, strings and `code_from_us`/`member_from_file` graphics check the exact bytes (or their SHA-1); `copy_us`, `tiles_from_file` and `tiles_from_us` check the bit depth and tile count; `tiles_from_png` checks that the image matches the sheet's tile grid, and `tile_range_from_png` that the range fits the sheet, both that every palette index is below the bit-depth limit; every replaced NARC member must keep its format, compression, bit depth, tile count and mapping; and the font fix checks the glyph size. Each fix can be left out of a build with `python3 work/tools/build.py --without <id>` (or built alone with `--only`). A fix whose `requires` names another fix only makes sense together with it; the build refuses to drop one without the other. Outside the message archives and these fixes, the only other bytes that differ from the Chinese ROM are container bookkeeping: the ROM header's layout fields, the FAT and the offset at 0x1000 where the RSA signature is stored move because ndspy rebuilds the ROM container around the changed files, not because of a fix.

Stages (and the order of this list): font → graphics → hardcoded strings → data and code patches. Offsets are file offsets; for arm9 and overlays that is the offset in the RAM image, so RAM = load address + offset (arm9 0x02000000; overlays from the y9 table, recorded in `work/patches/overlays.toml`). Decisions are ids in the decision register: `python3 work/tools/decisions.py show <id>`.

## font-glyphs

**Font: the USA … “ ” glyphs instead of the hack's 12-13 px ones**

- Kind: font
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: none
- Source: `work/patches/font-glyphs/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: in English text an ellipsis or a pair of double quotes shows as a wide gap ("Wait…" has a
double-width "…", and “quotes” stand apart from their words); lines with them can run past the edge of the
text box.

Technical: the hack redrew the ellipsis (code 0x01AF) and the curly double quotes (0x01B4, 0x01B5) of the
font NARC a/0/1/6 as CJK-width glyphs: 12 px wide in fonts 0, 1 and 2 and 13 px in font 4 (the hack's
redrawn Latin font), where the USA fonts have 6-7 px. In fonts 0-2 every other Latin glyph and width is
byte-identical to the USA ROM.
QA lays out the English against the vanilla widths and flags lines that only fit with them
(needs_vanilla_glyphs).

**What (old → new):**

Old: … “ ” are 12-13 px CJK-width glyphs in fonts 0, 1, 2 and 4.

New: the glyph bitmap and the width-table byte of these three codes are copied from the USA ROM's font
files 0, 1, 2 and 4, so they are the US glyphs again (6 px in fonts 0/1, 7 px in fonts 2/4). No other
glyph changes. build.py --glyph-fonts can narrow the font list; the verify step checks every restored glyph against the USA font.

**Evidence:**

- Decision pending: the question to the user to confirm the glyph restore is D-2042 in the main checkout's register; it is not yet in this branch's register, so this fix lists no decision of its own
- Related: D-0028 (quote-style rule, provisional) cites the hack's 12 px widths of “ ”
- work/notes/text_metrics.md: 'The hack's Latin is the vanilla Latin' (width table, recommendation)
- work/notes/integrity_audit_text.md: fonts row (only 01AF/01B4/01B5 differ from the hack)
- work/tools/qa.py: needs_vanilla_glyphs warning
- CHANGELOG.md v1.0.0: 'Restored the US glyphs for … “ ”, which the hack had widened to 12 px.'

**Touches:**

- `a/0/1/6` fonts 0, 1, 2, 4: glyph + width of 0x01AF, 0x01B4, 0x01B5 from the USA ROM

## gfx-battle-status-icons

**Battle HP-box status icons (PAR FRZ SLP PSN BRN)**

- Kind: graphics
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-1104, D-0768, D-1041
- Source: `work/patches/gfx-battle-status-icons/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: in every battle the status icon next to the HP bar reads 麻痹 冰冻 睡眠 中毒 灼伤.

Technical: these icons are not in any NARC: they are raw 4bpp tiles inside the battle overlay (pret
gBattleHpBar_RawGraphicComponents 41-55, 3 tiles each; hack overlay 14 = USA overlay 12), file offset
0x4C0A8, 480 bytes.

**What (old → new):**

Old: Chinese status abbreviations.

New: the 480 bytes are copied from the USA overlay 12 (0x36340), the same layout; the other 38 components are
identical apart from the hack's 'HP:'. Both ranges are checked by SHA-1 first.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/graphics_inventory.md: row 25 and 'Graphics inside code' (status_icons_battle_hpbox.png)

**Touches:**

- `overlay14+0x4C0A8` (RAM 0x0224C888), 480 bytes ← USA `overlay12+0x36340` (`code_from_us`)

## gfx-dex-header

**Pokédex header and bottom buttons**

- Kind: graphics
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-1110, D-1536, D-1541, D-1542, D-0281, D-0768
- Source: `work/patches/gfx-dex-header/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: the Pokédex top screen says 城都图鉴 / 全国图鉴 and the bottom-screen buttons read 搜索 打开 结束 叫声
详细 分布 大小 样子 返回.

Technical: a/0/6/8 #1 (header) and #4 (buttons) with their screens. A plain USA restore is impossible: the
hack shrank the region overlays #7/#8 to 80x24 px (they only cover the first two characters) and its area
page has five buttons where the USA has four. The search page copies #4 tiles 98/101 as the background of
its label windows, and screens 69/70/71 also draw #4.

**What (old → new):**

Old: Chinese header and buttons.

New: members generated by gfx.py make-dex-labels into the hack's layout: JOHTO / NATIONAL in USA letters
(NATIONAL condensed to 73 px) on the overlays, the USA POKéDEX plate part and NATIONAL ◀ ▶ JOHTO row on
screen #0, the USA buttons on the list page (#5/#6/#71), and AREA DATA SIZE FORMS BACK on the area page.
Re-tiling only reuses tiles no unchanged cell or code copy still shows (D-1536: the garbled search bars of
D-1505). The overhang of 'DEX' past the column is accepted (D-1541). Also in both costume copies.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/graphics_inventory.md: rows 12-13
- work/notes/graphics_layout_audit.md; work/graphics/layout_checks.json (runtime tile limits)

## gfx-naming-tabs

**Naming keyboard tab and button labels (ABC / abc / QWE, BACK / OK)**

- Kind: graphics
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: `naming-keyboard`
- Decisions: D-1039, D-1110, D-0768
- Source: `work/patches/gfx-naming-tabs/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: the naming screen's tabs and buttons are the Japanese labels かな / カナ / ＡＢＣ / もどる / おわり.

Technical: tiles 0-207 of the OBJ sheet #10 of data/namein.narc (identical in a/0/3/1 and the costume copies
data/clothes1|2/a031.narc) hold the tab and button labels. They must describe the pages as the code fix
naming-keyboard lays them out; without that fix tab 1 would read ABC over the pinyin page, hence the
requirement.

**What (old → new):**

Old: かな / カナ / ＡＢＣ / 1♪ tabs, もどる / おわり buttons.

New: tiles 0-207 come from naming_labels_en.png (gfx.py make-naming-labels): tab 1 (page 0, now ABC) shows
the hack's own 'ABC' tab art, カナ -> abc, tab 3 (now QWERTY) -> QWE, もどる / おわり -> the USA BACK / OK tiles
(same cells and palette). Composed labels kept by D-1110. Building --without gfx-naming-tabs (allowed)
leaves the Japanese かな tab label over the ABC page and ＡＢＣ over QWE.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/graphics_inventory.md: row 14
- work/notes/hardcoded_text.md: 'Naming keyboard (English)'
- work/build/screens/naming_fix_*.png (local)

**Touches:**

- `data/namein.narc` #10 (+ `a/0/3/1`, `data/clothes1/a031.narc`, `data/clothes2/a031.narc`): `tile_range_from_png` from naming_labels_en.png

## outfit-chooser-strings

**Outfit chooser labels (hardcoded in overlay 58)**

- Kind: strings
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-0830, D-0831
- Source: `work/patches/outfit-chooser-strings/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: in Oak's speech, after 'boy or girl', the outfit chooser lists 形象1 形象2 形象3 确认 in Chinese even
though all message text is English.

Technical: the hack's chooser (overlay 58, RAM 0x021E83C0, 0x7E0 bytes, no .bss) keeps its four labels as
0xFFFF-terminated strings inside the overlay, outside the message NARCs, packed back to back. The slots hold
2-3 characters. A ROM-wide scan (hardcoded.py scan) found no other player-facing Chinese outside the
message NARCs.

**What (old → new):**

Old: 确认 / 形象1 / 形象3 / 形象2 in overlay 58.

New: 'OK' is written in place. 'Outfit 1/2/3' do not fit their 3-character slots, so the armips source
(outfit-chooser-strings.asm) appends them to the end of overlay 58 (the overlay grows by 56 bytes, at most the
[[grow]] max of 64; the build updates its y9 ramSize), repoints the pointer words at +0x7C0/+0x7C4/+0x7C8 and
fills the old slots with 0xFFFF. The code copies each label into a String of capacity 16, so up to 15
characters are safe. The English lives in the asm and in the [[string]] `en` below (translators and the text
checks read it here); fixes.py check and the build refuse if they differ. The build also refuses if the ROM
no longer holds the Chinese, the growth passes the [[grow]] max, the overlay has .bss or another overlay starts
in the grown range.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/hardcoded_text.md: 'Survey' and 'Pipeline'
- In-game: work/build/screens/hardcoded_*.png (local): English labels, cursor works, OK leads to the naming screen
- work/tools/test_hardcoded.py: the scan finds exactly these 4 strings; test_asmpatch.py: the assembled overlay (golden SHA-1) and verify
- CHANGELOG.md v1.0.0: 'Hardcoded text outside the archives (the outfit chooser in overlay 58) is translated.'

**Touches:**

- `overlay58+0x6F0` (RAM 0x021E8AB0) (slot of 2 characters, pointers 0x4E4): 确认 → 'OK' (in place)
- `overlay58+0x6F6` (RAM 0x021E8AB6) (slot of 3 characters, pointers 0x7C0): 形象1 → 'Outfit 1' (relocated, at most 15 characters there)
- `overlay58+0x6FE` (RAM 0x021E8ABE) (slot of 3 characters, pointers 0x7C8): 形象3 → 'Outfit 3' (relocated, at most 15 characters there)
- `overlay58+0x706` (RAM 0x021E8AC6) (slot of 3 characters, pointers 0x7C4): 形象2 → 'Outfit 2' (relocated, at most 15 characters there)
- `overlay58`: may grow by up to 64 bytes (appended at its end)

**Source** (`work/patches/outfit-chooser-strings/outfit-chooser-strings.asm`, armips; the new bytes):

<details>
<summary>outfit-chooser-strings.asm</summary>

```asm
; outfit-chooser-strings - English labels in the outfit chooser of Oak's speech (overlay 58). D-0830, D-0831.
; Why and what: fix.toml next to this file; overview work/patches/FIXES.md; work/notes/hardcoded_text.md.
;
; The hack's outfit chooser (overlay 58, RAM 0x021E83C0, 0x7E0 bytes, no .bss) keeps its four list labels
; inside the overlay, as 0xFFFF-terminated strings packed back to back. The code copies each label into a
; String of capacity 16 (String_New(0x10) + CopyU16ArrayToString), so a label may have 15 characters.
;   确认   confirm, last list item   slot of 2 characters   loaded from the literal pool at +0x4E4
;   形象1/3/2  outfit 1, 3, 2         slots of 3 characters  read through the pointer table at +0x7C0
; 'OK' fits its slot and is written in place. 'Outfit 1/2/3' do not fit, so they are appended to the end of
; the overlay, the pointer table is repointed and the old slots are blanked. The overlay grows from 0x7E0 to
; 0x818 bytes; fix.toml [[grow]] allows 64, and the build updates its ramSize in the y9 overlay table.
;
; The English here must equal `en` of the [[string]] entries in fix.toml (translators and the text checks
; read it there): fixes.py check compares the literals, the build compares the bytes.

.nds
.include "../include/guards.inc"
.loadtable "../include/charmap.tbl", "UTF-8"     ; .string: game character codes, 0xFFFF end

.definelabel OutfitChooser_ConfirmLabelRef, 0x021E88A4   ; +0x4E4: u16 *, ldr'd for the 确认 item
.definelabel OutfitChooser_ConfirmLabel,    0x021E8AB0   ; +0x6F0: u16[3] 确认
.definelabel OutfitChooser_Outfit1Label,    0x021E8AB6   ; +0x6F6: u16[4] 形象1
.definelabel OutfitChooser_Outfit3Label,    0x021E8ABE   ; +0x6FE: u16[4] 形象3
.definelabel OutfitChooser_Outfit2Label,    0x021E8AC6   ; +0x706: u16[4] 形象2
.definelabel OutfitChooser_OutfitLabels,    0x021E8B80   ; +0x7C0: u16 *[3], list items 1, 2, 3
.definelabel Overlay58_End,                 0x021E8BA0   ; +0x7E0: end of the hack's overlay

.open "overlay58.bin", 0x021E83C0

; 确认 -> OK, in place. Its pointer stays.
expect32_abs OutfitChooser_ConfirmLabelRef, OutfitChooser_ConfirmLabel
.org OutfitChooser_ConfirmLabel
.area 3 * 2
    expect32_at 0, 0x0BB809B9                     ; 确认
    expect16_at 4, 0xFFFF
    .string "OK"
.endarea

; 形象1, 形象3, 形象2: the English is too long for these slots and moves to the end of the overlay.
.org OutfitChooser_Outfit1Label
.area 3 * 8
    expect32_at  0, 0x0BFB05C5                    ; 形象
    expect32_at  4, 0xFFFF0122                    ;     1
    expect32_at  8, 0x0BFB05C5                    ; 形象
    expect32_at 12, 0xFFFF0124                    ;     3
    expect32_at 16, 0x0BFB05C5                    ; 形象
    expect32_at 20, 0xFFFF0123                    ;     2
    .fill 3 * 8, 0xFF                             ; blank (0xFFFF: empty strings)
.endarea

.org OutfitChooser_OutfitLabels
.area 3 * 4
    expect32_at 0, OutfitChooser_Outfit1Label
    expect32_at 4, OutfitChooser_Outfit2Label
    expect32_at 8, OutfitChooser_Outfit3Label
    .word Outfit1Label_EN, Outfit2Label_EN, Outfit3Label_EN
.endarea

; Appended to the overlay, in the hack's order (1, 3, 2).
.org Overlay58_End
.area 64                                          ; fix.toml [[grow]] max
    expect_end
Outfit1Label_EN:
    .string "Outfit 1"
Outfit3Label_EN:
    .string "Outfit 3"
Outfit2Label_EN:
    .string "Outfit 2"
    .align 4, 0xFF                                ; the overlay stays a multiple of 4 bytes
.endarea

.close
```

</details>

## pcbox-name-width

**PC box header: species-name window wide enough for 10 characters**

- Kind: data
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-1537, D-1511
- Source: `work/patches/pcbox-name-width/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: on the PC box top screen the last letter of a 10-character species name or nickname is cut off at
the gender icon: 'Charmeleon' shows as 'Charmeleor'.

Technical: the hack's (Japanese-base) window template table in overlay 16 (0x12E9C, 8 bytes per window:
bg, x, y, w, h, pal, base tile) makes the species-name window 7 tiles (56 px) wide. Chinese names are at
most 5 characters, so the hack never needed more; English names are up to 10 (D-0858).

**What (old → new):**

Old: name window 04 08 05 07 (56 px); the following bg-4 windows start at base tiles 0x69, 0x77, ...

New: the USA values: name window 04 08 05 08 (64 px, ending at the gender icon at x 128), and the base tiles
of the later bg-4 windows move up by 2 (0x77 -> 0x79 ... 0x107 -> 0x109), so bg-4 tiles run to 288 as in the
USA ROM. Templates [0]-[8] and [17]-[19] equal the USA overlay 14 table (0x12BB4, 0x12C3C). Nothing else on the screen changes.

**Evidence:**

- D-1511 (emulator, 2026-10-05): 'Charmeleon' in full before the gender icon, rest of the box screen unchanged; screens work/build/harness/hunt_ui/box_party_pair.png (local)
- git e18d0f9 'Fix increment 4: Pokédex button/header graphics pipeline, PC box name window'

**Touches:**

- `overlay16+0x12E9C` (RAM 0x021F781C) `pcbox-header-name-width`: 72 bytes, was `0804 0705 0F02 0069 … (36 halfwords)`
- `overlay16+0x12F24` (RAM 0x021F78A4) `pcbox-header-name-width-2`: 24 bytes, was `0104 080B 0F02 00E1 … (12 halfwords)`

**Source** (`work/patches/pcbox-name-width/pcbox-name-width.asm`, armips; the new bytes):

<details>
<summary>pcbox-name-width.asm</summary>

```asm
; pcbox-name-width - PC box header: species-name window wide enough for 10 characters. D-1537, D-1511.
; Why and what: fix.toml next to this file; overview work/patches/FIXES.md.
;
; The PC box top screen builds its windows from a WindowTemplate table in overlay 16 (8 bytes each:
; bg, x, y, width, height, palette, base tile; all in tiles). The hack (Japanese base) makes the
; species-name window 7 tiles (56 px) wide, so 'Charmeleon' shows as 'Charmeleor'. The new values are
; the USA ones (US overlay 14: 0x12BB4 for [0]-[8], 0x12C3C for [17]-[19]): the name window is 8 tiles
; (64 px, ending at the gender icon at x 128), and the bg-4 windows after it move their first tile up
; by 2, so bg-4 tiles run to 288 as in the USA ROM. Nothing else on the screen changes.

.nds
.thumb
.include "../include/guards.inc"

.definelabel PcBox_TopScreenWindows, 0x021F781C   ; WindowTemplate[22] (overlay 16 + 0x12E9C)

; struct WindowTemplate { u8 bg, x, y, width, height, palette; u16 baseTile; }
.macro window, bg, x, y, w, h, pal, base
  .byte bg, x, y, w, h, pal
  .halfword base
.endmacro

; The template at the current address is this one.
.macro window_was, bg, x, y, w, h, pal, base
  expect32_at 0, (bg) | (x) << 8 | (y) << 16 | (w) << 24
  expect32_at 4, (h) | (pal) << 8 | (base) << 16
.endmacro

.open "overlay16.bin", 0x021E4980

;                                  bg   x   y   w  h  pal  base
.org PcBox_TopScreenWindows + 0 * 8
.area 9 * 8
    window_was                      4,  8,  5,  7, 2, 15, 0x069   ; [0] species name: 7 tiles
    window                          4,  8,  5,  8, 2, 15, 0x069   ;     -> 8 tiles (64 px)
    window_was                      4,  1,  7,  8, 2, 15, 0x077   ; [1]
    window                          4,  1,  7,  8, 2, 15, 0x079   ;     base + 2
    window_was                      4,  4,  9,  6, 2, 15, 0x087   ; [2]
    window                          4,  4,  9,  6, 2, 15, 0x089
    window_was                      4,  1,  0, 30, 3, 15, 0x00F   ; [3] unchanged (its tiles come before the name)
    window                          4,  1,  0, 30, 3, 15, 0x00F
    window_was                      4, 16,  5,  2, 2, 15, 0x093   ; [4]
    window                          4, 16,  5,  2, 2, 15, 0x095
    window_was                      4,  1,  5,  6, 2, 15, 0x097   ; [5]
    window                          4,  1,  5,  6, 2, 15, 0x099
    window_was                      4,  1, 13,  8, 2, 15, 0x0A3   ; [6]
    window                          4,  1, 13,  8, 2, 15, 0x0A5
    window_was                      4,  1, 17, 11, 2, 15, 0x0B3   ; [7]
    window                          4,  1, 17, 11, 2, 15, 0x0B5
    window_was                      4,  1, 21, 12, 2, 15, 0x0C9   ; [8]
    window                          4,  1, 21, 12, 2, 15, 0x0CB
.endarea

; [9]-[16] are bg-6 windows: unchanged. The second bg-4 group follows.
.org PcBox_TopScreenWindows + 17 * 8
.area 3 * 8
    window_was                      4,  1, 11,  8, 2, 15, 0x0E1   ; [17]
    window                          4,  1, 11,  8, 2, 15, 0x0E3
    window_was                      4,  1, 15, 11, 2, 15, 0x0F1   ; [18]
    window                          4,  1, 15, 11, 2, 15, 0x0F3
    window_was                      4,  1, 19, 12, 2, 15, 0x107   ; [19]
    window                          4,  1, 19, 12, 2, 15, 0x109
.endarea

.close
```

</details>

## ivev-panel

**Summary IV/EV panel: the IV column clears the English stat labels**

- Kind: code
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-1574
- Source: `work/patches/ivev-panel/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: on the summary stats page, L opens the hack's IV/EV panel. The English stat labels run into the IV
column: 'Sp. Atk' covers the first digit (an IV of 31 reads '81') and 'Attack' touches it. The Chinese labels
are two characters and leave room.

Technical: the panel is drawn by the hack's arm9 routine 0x0208C1A8 (called only from the summary screen).
It prints the IV numbers right-aligned by 0x0208C154 at x = r2 + 24 with r2 = 0x1A, so their right edge is at
x 50; the widest English label 'Defense' is 41 px.

**What (old → new):**

Old: IV numbers end at x 50, the 'IVs' header starts at x 0x22.

New: 'movs r2, #0x1A' -> 'movs r2, #0x20' at 0x0208C262 moves the IV column 6 px right (two-digit IVs clear
'Defense' by 3 px), and 'movs r3, #0x22' -> '#0x28' at 0x0208C1E2 moves the 'IVs' header with it. The labels
(0295 #110-115) and the EV column (r2 = 0x40) are unchanged.

**Evidence:**

- D-1574: emu_harness.py vqueue --case buttons, work/build/harness/verifyqueue/en/buttons_m*_L.png (local)
- git c7d2c29 'Code: summary IV/EV panel IV column clears the English stat labels (D-1574)'

**Touches:**

- `arm9+0x8C262` (RAM 0x0208C262) `ivev-panel-iv-x`: 2 bytes, was `221A`
- `arm9+0x8C1E2` (RAM 0x0208C1E2) `ivev-panel-iv-header-x`: 2 bytes, was `2322`

**Source** (`work/patches/ivev-panel/ivev-panel.asm`, armips; the new bytes):

<details>
<summary>ivev-panel.asm</summary>

```asm
; ivev-panel - Summary IV/EV panel: the IV column clears the English stat labels. D-1574.
; Why and what: fix.toml next to this file; overview work/patches/FIXES.md.
;
; L on the summary stats page opens the hack's IV/EV panel, drawn by the hack's arm9 routine 0x0208C1A8
; (called only from the summary screen, at 0x02087EDC, 0x02088130 and 0x02089744). It prints the IV numbers
; right-aligned by 0x0208C154 at x = r2 + 24. With r2 = 0x1A they end at x 50, and the English labels
; ('Sp. Atk', 'Defense' = 41 px; bank 0295 #110-115, shared with the stats page) run into them.
; Both edits move the IV column and its header 6 px right. The labels and the EV column (r2 = 0x40 at
; 0x0208C278, 'EVs' header x 0x43 at 0x0208C210) are unchanged.

.nds
.thumb
.include "../include/guards.inc"

IV_SHIFT equ 6                  ; px: two-digit IVs clear 'Defense' by 3 px

.open "arm9.bin", 0x02000000

.org 0x0208C1E2                 ; the 'IVs' header (0295 #195)
.area 2
    expect16 0x2322             ; mov r3, #0x22   (x)
    mov     r3, #0x22 + IV_SHIFT
.endarea

.org 0x0208C262                 ; the IV numbers
.area 2
    expect16 0x221A             ; mov r2, #0x1A   (x - 24 of the right edge)
    mov     r2, #0x1A + IV_SHIFT
.endarea

.close
```

</details>

## msgload

**Text banks are read line by line (fixes the summary and bag memory crashes)**

- Kind: code
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-1390, D-1002
- Source: `work/patches/msgload/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players (rc3): switching Pokémon on the summary screen's skills page crashed the game (melonDS crash,
DeSmuME hang); the bag was 108 bytes from the same crash. The untouched Chinese ROM does not crash with the
same save, so this is caused by the translation, not a hack bug.

Technical: each screen gets a fixed-size heap, and many screens load whole message banks into it
(NewMsgDataFromNarc type 0, arm9 0x0200BA98). The English banks are 1.5-3x the size of the Chinese ones:
on the summary screen (heap 19) banks 0295 and 0739 grew by 3,056 and 11,790 bytes and the spare room went
from 208 to -124 bytes. The failed allocation returns NULL, the next file read goes to address 0, which
mirrors ITCM, and overwrites the interrupt handler at 0x01FF8000.

**What (old → new):**

Old: callers choose type 0 (whole bank into the screen heap) or type 1 (a NARC handle that reads each line
when asked); 149 call sites use type 0.

New: msgload-all makes NewMsgDataFromNarc always store type 1 ('adds r5, r0, #0' -> 'movs r5, #1' at
0x0200BA9A), so no screen loads a whole bank any more. Every MsgData function handles both types and nothing
outside them reads a loaded bank. The same change at the five measured call sites (summary 0295/0739, bag
0010/0219/0739: 'movs r0, #0' -> '#1') is kept as a second layer. Same text; only where it is read from.
Spare room: summary 208 -> 10,376 bytes, bag 108 -> 55,540.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/heap_audit.md: crash class, fix and results table
- work/tools/memcheck.py run, scenarios summary, summary_full, bag, bag_full (work/tools/memcheck_scenarios.json): no failed allocation, no heap below 4 KB more than 256 bytes under the Chinese figure
- CHANGELOG.md v1.0.0-rc4: 'Crash when switching Pokémon on the summary screen's skills page, and a bag that was 108 bytes from the same crash.'

**Touches:**

- `arm9+0x8799A` (RAM 0x0208799A) `msgload-summary-0295`: 2 bytes, was `2000`
- `arm9+0x87A0C` (RAM 0x02087A0C) `msgload-summary-0739`: 2 bytes, was `2000`
- `overlay17+0x940` (RAM 0x021F9020) `msgload-bag-0010`: 2 bytes, was `2000`
- `overlay17+0x970` (RAM 0x021F9050) `msgload-bag-0219`: 2 bytes, was `2000`
- `overlay17+0x982` (RAM 0x021F9062) `msgload-bag-0739`: 2 bytes, was `2000`
- `arm9+0xBA9A` (RAM 0x0200BA9A) `msgload-all`: 2 bytes, was `1C05`

**Source** (`work/patches/msgload/msgload.asm`, armips; the new bytes):

<details>
<summary>msgload.asm</summary>

```asm
; msgload - Text banks are read line by line (fixes the summary and bag memory crashes). D-1390, D-1002.
; Why and what: fix.toml next to this file; overview work/patches/FIXES.md; work/notes/heap_audit.md.
;
; NewMsgDataFromNarc(type, narc, bank, heap) (hack arm9 0x0200BA98) loads a message bank in one of two ways:
;   MSGDATA_LOAD_DIRECT (0)  the whole bank is read into the caller's heap
;   MSGDATA_LOAD_LAZY   (1)  a NARC handle; each line is read when it is asked for
; The English banks are 1.5-3x the size of the Chinese ones, so screens with a fixed-size heap that load
; whole banks ran out of memory (summary screen: -124 bytes, then a write through NULL into ITCM).
; Every MsgData function handles both types, and nothing outside them reads a loaded bank, so type 1 is
; safe everywhere. Same text; only where it is read from.

.nds
.thumb
.include "../include/guards.inc"

MSGDATA_LOAD_LAZY equ 1

.open "arm9.bin", 0x02000000

; All screens: NewMsgDataFromNarc keeps type 1 whatever the caller asked for (149 call sites used 0 in rc3).
.org 0x0200BA9A
.area 2
    expect16 0x1C05             ; add r5, r0, #0   (r5 = type)
    mov     r5, #MSGDATA_LOAD_LAZY
.endarea

; Second layer, kept in case the line above is ever dropped: the five call sites that were measured
; (memcheck.py) pass type 1 themselves.

.org 0x0208799A                 ; summary screen (heap 19): bank 0295, summary labels, 6916 -> 9972 bytes in English (call at 0x020879A0)
.area 2
    expect16 0x2000             ; mov r0, #0
    mov     r0, #MSGDATA_LOAD_LAZY
.endarea

.org 0x02087A0C                 ; summary screen (heap 19): bank 0739, move names, 15226 -> 27016 bytes (call at 0x02087A12)
.area 2
    expect16 0x2000             ; mov r0, #0
    mov     r0, #MSGDATA_LOAD_LAZY
.endarea

.close

.open "overlay17.bin", 0x021F86E0  ; the bag

.org 0x021F9020                 ; bag (heap 6): bank 0010, bag labels (call at 0x021F9028)
.area 2
    expect16 0x2000             ; mov r0, #0
    mov     r0, #MSGDATA_LOAD_LAZY
.endarea

.org 0x021F9050                 ; bag (heap 6): bank 0219, item names, 14252 -> 22524 bytes (call at 0x021F9058)
.area 2
    expect16 0x2000             ; mov r0, #0
    mov     r0, #MSGDATA_LOAD_LAZY
.endarea

.org 0x021F9062                 ; bag (heap 6): bank 0739, move names for the TM pocket; bank = 0xBE*4-0x15 (call at 0x021F906A)
.area 2
    expect16 0x2000             ; mov r0, #0
    mov     r0, #MSGDATA_LOAD_LAZY
.endarea

.close
```

</details>

## namelen

**Name lengths: US limits (7 characters for trainers, 10 for Pokémon)**

- Kind: code
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-0858
- Source: `work/patches/namelen/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: the naming screen stops after 5 characters, so most English names and nicknames do not fit
("Charlie", "Charmeleon").

Technical: the hack is built on the Japanese HeartGold (game code IPKJ). Every naming-screen call passes
maxLen = 5: the direct calls of NamingScreen_CreateArgs (hack 0x02081DA4) for the player and rival in Oak's
speech (overlay 49), the egg hatch nickname and naming kind 7, and the script commands' calls of
CallTask_NamingScreen (hack 0x0203EDEC) for the player, rival, nickname (gift Pokémon, Name Rater) and group
name. The save buffers already have the US sizes, so only the limit is Japanese.

**What (old → new):**

Old: maxLen 5 at all 8 call sites: seven pass the literal 5 ('movs r3, #5'), the group-name site passes
r1, which holds 5 there ('adds r3, r1, #0').

New: the USA values: 7 for the player, rival, group name and kind 7; 10 for the two Pokémon nickname
call sites. Each patch changes one immediate ('movs r3, #5' -> '#7' / '#10'; the group-name site
'adds r3, r1, #0' -> 'movs r3, #7'). Box names (8) are unchanged. There is no battle-capture nickname call:
the hack removed that prompt (D-1040). Default names (bank 0247) are 5 characters or fewer and need no change.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/hardcoded_text.md: 'Name lengths' (call-site table, default names)
- In-game check by the user in melonDS: 7-character trainer names, 10-character nicknames (D-0858)
- CHANGELOG.md v1.0.0: 'Name lengths restored to US limits: 7 characters for trainers, 10 for Pokémon'

**Touches:**

- `overlay49+0x4E` (RAM 0x021E49CE) `namelen-player-intro`: 2 bytes, was `2305`
- `overlay49+0x66` (RAM 0x021E49E6) `namelen-rival-intro`: 2 bytes, was `2305`
- `arm9+0x42862` (RAM 0x02042862) `namelen-player-script`: 2 bytes, was `2305`
- `arm9+0x42892` (RAM 0x02042892) `namelen-rival-script`: 2 bytes, was `2305`
- `arm9+0x4291E` (RAM 0x0204291E) `namelen-nickname-script`: 2 bytes, was `2305`
- `arm9+0x90944` (RAM 0x02090944) `namelen-nickname-egg`: 2 bytes, was `2305`
- `arm9+0x490DA` (RAM 0x020490DA) `namelen-group-script`: 2 bytes, was `1C0B`
- `overlay44+0x2E6C` (RAM 0x02228DAC) `namelen-kind7`: 2 bytes, was `2305`

**Source** (`work/patches/namelen/namelen.asm`, armips; the new bytes):

<details>
<summary>namelen.asm</summary>

```asm
; namelen - Name lengths: US limits (7 characters for trainers, 10 for Pokémon). D-0858.
; Why and what: fix.toml next to this file; overview work/patches/FIXES.md.
;
; The hack is built on the Japanese HeartGold, so every naming-screen call passes maxLen = 5 in r3:
; the direct calls of NamingScreen_CreateArgs (hack 0x02081DA4, US 0x020830D8) in Oak's speech, the
; egg hatch and kind 7, and the script commands' calls of CallTask_NamingScreen (hack 0x0203EDEC).
; The save buffers already have the US sizes; only the limit is Japanese. Each edit below changes the
; one instruction that loads maxLen.
; Box names (8) are unchanged; the hack has no battle-capture nickname prompt (D-1040).

.nds
.thumb
.include "../include/guards.inc"

TRAINER_NAME_LEN equ 7          ; US PLAYER_NAME_LENGTH: player, rival, group, kind 7
POKEMON_NAME_LEN equ 10         ; US POKEMON_NAME_LENGTH: nicknames

; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
; Oak's speech (hack overlay 49; US overlay 53)
.open "overlay49.bin", 0x021E4980

.org 0x021E49CE                 ; NamingScreen_CreateArgs(heap, NAME_SCREEN_PLAYER, 0, maxLen)
.area 2
    expect16 0x2305             ; mov r3, #5
    mov     r3, #TRAINER_NAME_LEN
.endarea

.org 0x021E49E6                 ; NamingScreen_CreateArgs(heap, NAME_SCREEN_RIVAL, 0, maxLen)
.area 2
    expect16 0x2305             ; mov r3, #5
    mov     r3, #TRAINER_NAME_LEN
.endarea

.close

; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
; Script commands and the egg hatch (arm9)
.open "arm9.bin", 0x02000000

.org 0x02042862                 ; script 'name player': CallTask_NamingScreen(.., PLAYER, 0, maxLen) (US 0x020431D6)
.area 2
    expect16 0x2305             ; mov r3, #5
    mov     r3, #TRAINER_NAME_LEN
.endarea

.org 0x02042892                 ; script 'name rival'
.area 2
    expect16 0x2305             ; mov r3, #5
    mov     r3, #TRAINER_NAME_LEN
.endarea

.org 0x0204291E                 ; script 'nickname Pokémon': gift/starter Pokémon, Name Rater (US 0x02043292)
.area 2
    expect16 0x2305             ; mov r3, #5
    mov     r3, #POKEMON_NAME_LEN
.endarea

.org 0x020490DA                 ; script 'name group' (kind 5): r1 holds 5 here
.area 2
    expect16 0x1C0B             ; add r3, r1, #0   (maxLen = r1 = 5)
    mov     r3, #TRAINER_NAME_LEN
.endarea

.org 0x02090944                 ; egg hatch: CreateArgs(heap, NAME_SCREEN_POKEMON, species, maxLen) (US 0x020911C4)
.area 2
    expect16 0x2305             ; mov r3, #5
    mov     r3, #POKEMON_NAME_LEN
.endarea

.close

; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
; Naming kind 7 (hack overlay 44; US overlay 43 0x0222CD5C; pret calls it NAME_SCREEN_UNK7)
.open "overlay44.bin", 0x02225F40

.org 0x02228DAC                 ; NamingScreen_CreateArgs(heap, 7, 0, maxLen)
.area 2
    expect16 0x2305             ; mov r3, #5
    mov     r3, #TRAINER_NAME_LEN
.endarea

.close
```

## naming-keyboard

**English naming keyboard: ABC page first, pinyin IME off**

- Kind: code
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Required by: `gfx-naming-tabs`
- Decisions: D-1039, D-1002
- Source: `work/patches/naming-keyboard/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: the naming screen opens on a pinyin input page: typed letters turn into Chinese character
candidates, so an English name cannot be typed there. The hack's ＡＢＣ page types full-width letters that
look spaced out in every dialogue that shows the name.

Technical: the hack's keyboard (Japanese base) has four tabs; page N uses the rows sKeyboardLayoutPtrs[N]
(arm9 0x0210F688, 13 keys + 0xFFFF per row). Page 0 (the page the screen opens on) runs the hack's pinyin
IME from the key handler at 0x02083814 ('cmp r0, #0; bne 0x02083CF8' at 0x02083C22: keys on page 0 go into
the pinyin buffer at data+0x5E4, candidates from a/0/3/1 #19/#20). Page 2 holds the full-width codes
0x00AC-0x00DF, whose glyphs are 9-11 px wide in message fonts 1/2/4 (Western letters 6-7 px).

**What (old → new):**

Old: tab 1 (page 0) = pinyin IME, tab 2 = a-z/A-Z/0-9 (Western), tab 3 = full-width ＡＢＣ, tab 4 = 1/♪.

New: 'bne' -> 'b' at 0x02083C24, so every page inserts keys directly and the IME never starts.
Tab 1 (page 0, still the default) = ABC: the hack's own ABC layout (A-M, N-Z, a-m, n-z, 0-9 . , space) in
Western codes 0x0121-0x015E. Tab 3 (page 2) = QWE: blank row, 1-0, QWERTYUIOP, ASDFGHJKL ’ -, ZXCVBNM , .
(’ is the apostrophe of the game font, 0x01B3; there is no straight ' key.)
Tabs 2 and 4 are the hack's. Putting ABC on page 0 makes it the default without touching the init code
(changing the default page would need 5+ patches). The tab labels are fix gfx-naming-tabs, which requires
this fix; building --without gfx-naming-tabs keeps the hack's Japanese tab art, so the かな label sits over
the ABC page and ＡＢＣ over the QWE page.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/hardcoded_text.md: 'Naming keyboard (English)'
- DeSmuME check: work/build/screens/naming_fix_*.png (local): opens on ABC, every tab types, the dialogue shows 'Your name is An1zQ5!?'
- CHANGELOG.md v1.0.0: 'Naming keyboard: the Chinese pinyin input is removed, and the keyboard opens on ABC. The tabs are ABC / abc / QWE / 1♪.'

**Touches:**

- `arm9+0x83C24` (RAM 0x02083C24) `naming-ime-off`: 2 bytes, was `D168`
- `arm9+0x100CE4` (RAM 0x02100CE4) `naming-abc-row1`: 26 bytes, was `01DE 01DE 01DE 01DE … (13 halfwords)`
- `arm9+0x100D00` (RAM 0x02100D00) `naming-abc-row2`: 26 bytes, was `01DE 01DE 01DE 01DE … (13 halfwords)`
- `arm9+0x100D1C` (RAM 0x02100D1C) `naming-abc-row3`: 26 bytes, was `013B 0141 012F 013C … (13 halfwords)`
- `arm9+0x100C90` (RAM 0x02100C90) `naming-abc-row4`: 26 bytes, was `01DE 012B 013D 012E … (13 halfwords)`
- `arm9+0x100CC8` (RAM 0x02100CC8) `naming-abc-row5`: 26 bytes, was `01DE 01DE 0144 0142 … (13 halfwords)`
- `arm9+0x100DFC` (RAM 0x02100DFC) `naming-qwe-row1`: 26 bytes, was `00AC 00AD 00AE 00AF … (13 halfwords)`
- `arm9+0x100E34` (RAM 0x02100E34) `naming-qwe-row2`: 26 bytes, was `00B9 00BA 00BB 00BC … (13 halfwords)`
- `arm9+0x100E50` (RAM 0x02100E50) `naming-qwe-row3`: 26 bytes, was `00C6 00C7 00C8 00C9 … (13 halfwords)`
- `arm9+0x100E6C` (RAM 0x02100E6C) `naming-qwe-row4`: 26 bytes, was `00D3 00D4 00D5 00D6 … (13 halfwords)`
- `arm9+0x100EA4` (RAM 0x02100EA4) `naming-qwe-row5`: 26 bytes, was `00A2 00A3 00A4 00A5 … (13 halfwords)`

**Source** (`work/patches/naming-keyboard/naming-keyboard.asm`, armips; the new bytes):

<details>
<summary>naming-keyboard.asm</summary>

```asm
; naming-keyboard - English naming keyboard: ABC page first, pinyin IME off. D-1039, D-1002.
; Why and what: fix.toml next to this file; overview work/patches/FIXES.md.
; The tab labels (ABC / abc / QWE) are the graphics fix gfx-naming-tabs, which requires this fix.
;
; The hack's keyboard (Japanese base) has four tabs. Page N types the keys of the rows
; sKeyboardLayoutPtrs[N][0..4] (5 row pointers per page); a row is 13 key codes and an 0xFFFF end.
; The screen opens on page 0, which ran the hack's pinyin IME; page 2 typed full-width letters.
;
;   tab  page  hack                                  now
;   1    0     pinyin IME (QWERTY into a pinyin       ABC: A-M, N-Z, a-m, n-z, 0-9 . ,
;              buffer, hanzi candidates in rows 1-2)
;   2    1     a-z / A-Z / 0-9                        unchanged (abc)
;   3    2     full-width ＡＢＣ, ａｂｃ, ０-９            QWE: blank, 1-0, QWERTYUIOP, ASDFGHJKL ’ -, ZXCVBNM , .
;   4    3     1/♪ symbols                            unchanged
;
; Putting ABC on page 0 makes it the default without touching the init code (changing the default
; page would need 5+ patches).

.nds
.thumb
.include "../include/guards.inc"
.include "../include/charmap.inc"

.definelabel sKeyboardLayoutPtrs, 0x0210F688     ; const u16 *[4 pages][5 rows]
.definelabel NamingScreen_InsertKey, 0x02083CF8  ; the normal "insert key" path of the key handler

; The current address is row `row` of page `page`: the pointer table points here.
.macro keyboard_row, page, row
  expect32_abs sKeyboardLayoutPtrs + 4 * ((page) * 5 + (row)), org()
.endmacro

; The 13 keys at the current address are k0..k12, and the row ends with 0xFFFF.
.macro keys_were, k0, k1, k2, k3, k4, k5, k6, k7, k8, k9, k10, k11, k12
  expect16_at  0, k0
  expect16_at  2, k1
  expect16_at  4, k2
  expect16_at  6, k3
  expect16_at  8, k4
  expect16_at 10, k5
  expect16_at 12, k6
  expect16_at 14, k7
  expect16_at 16, k8
  expect16_at 18, k9
  expect16_at 20, k10
  expect16_at 22, k11
  expect16_at 24, k12
  expect16_at 26, 0xFFFF
.endmacro

; Write 13 keys; the row's 0xFFFF end stays.
.macro keys, k0, k1, k2, k3, k4, k5, k6, k7, k8, k9, k10, k11, k12
  .area 26
    .halfword k0, k1, k2, k3, k4, k5, k6, k7, k8, k9, k10, k11, k12
  .endarea
.endmacro

.open "arm9.bin", 0x02000000

; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
; IME off. In the key handler (hack 0x02083814, US NamingScreen_HandleCharacterInput),
; 'cmp r0, #0; bne NamingScreen_InsertKey' sends keys on pages 1-3 to the normal insert path and keys
; on page 0 into the hack's pinyin IME (pinyin buffer at data+0x5E4, candidate lookup 0x020835E4 over
; a/0/3/1 #19/#20). An unconditional branch makes every page insert the key directly; the IME never
; starts. Keys >= 0x1FF (hanzi) would still take the hack's commit path, but no page has them any more.
.org 0x02083C24
.area 2
    expect16_at -2, 0x2800      ; cmp r0, #0   (r0 = page != 0)
    expect16 0xD168             ; bne NamingScreen_InsertKey
    b       NamingScreen_InsertKey
.endarea

; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
; Tab 1 / page 0 (opens first): pinyin page -> ABC, the hack's own ABC layout in Western codes.

.org 0x02100CE4
    keyboard_row 0, 0           ; was: pinyin candidate row 1 (blank)
    keys_were CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE
    keys CH_A, CH_B, CH_C, CH_D, CH_E, CH_F, CH_G, CH_H, CH_I, CH_J, CH_K, CH_L, CH_M

.org 0x02100D00
    keyboard_row 0, 1           ; was: pinyin candidate row 2 (blank)
    keys_were CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE
    keys CH_N, CH_O, CH_P, CH_Q, CH_R, CH_S, CH_T, CH_U, CH_V, CH_W, CH_X, CH_Y, CH_Z

.org 0x02100D1C
    keyboard_row 0, 2           ; was: Q W E R T Y U I O P _ _ _
    keys_were CH_Q, CH_W, CH_E, CH_R, CH_T, CH_Y, CH_U, CH_I, CH_O, CH_P, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE
    keys CH_LC_A, CH_LC_B, CH_LC_C, CH_LC_D, CH_LC_E, CH_LC_F, CH_LC_G, CH_LC_H, CH_LC_I, CH_LC_J, CH_LC_K, CH_LC_L, CH_LC_M

.org 0x02100C90
    keyboard_row 0, 3           ; was: _ A S D F G H J K L _ and the candidate arrows ← →
    keys_were CH_SPACE, CH_A, CH_S, CH_D, CH_F, CH_G, CH_H, CH_J, CH_K, CH_L, CH_SPACE, CH_ARROW_LEFT, CH_ARROW_RIGHT
    keys CH_LC_N, CH_LC_O, CH_LC_P, CH_LC_Q, CH_LC_R, CH_LC_S, CH_LC_T, CH_LC_U, CH_LC_V, CH_LC_W, CH_LC_X, CH_LC_Y, CH_LC_Z

.org 0x02100CC8
    keyboard_row 0, 4           ; was: _ _ Z X C V B N M _ _ _ _
    keys_were CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_Z, CH_X, CH_C, CH_V, CH_B, CH_N, CH_M, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE
    keys CH_0, CH_1, CH_2, CH_3, CH_4, CH_5, CH_6, CH_7, CH_8, CH_9, CH_PERIOD, CH_COMMA, CH_SPACE

; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
; Tab 3 / page 2: full-width ＡＢＣ -> QWE (QWERTY in Western codes).

.org 0x02100DFC
    keyboard_row 2, 0           ; was: Ａ-Ｍ
    keys_were FW_A, FW_B, FW_C, FW_D, FW_E, FW_F, FW_G, FW_H, FW_I, FW_J, FW_K, FW_L, FW_M
    keys CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE

.org 0x02100E34
    keyboard_row 2, 1           ; was: Ｎ-Ｚ
    keys_were FW_N, FW_O, FW_P, FW_Q, FW_R, FW_S, FW_T, FW_U, FW_V, FW_W, FW_X, FW_Y, FW_Z
    keys CH_1, CH_2, CH_3, CH_4, CH_5, CH_6, CH_7, CH_8, CH_9, CH_0, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE

.org 0x02100E50
    keyboard_row 2, 2           ; was: ａ-ｍ
    keys_were FW_LC_A, FW_LC_B, FW_LC_C, FW_LC_D, FW_LC_E, FW_LC_F, FW_LC_G, FW_LC_H, FW_LC_I, FW_LC_J, FW_LC_K, FW_LC_L, FW_LC_M
    keys CH_Q, CH_W, CH_E, CH_R, CH_T, CH_Y, CH_U, CH_I, CH_O, CH_P, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE

.org 0x02100E6C
    keyboard_row 2, 3           ; was: ｎ-ｚ
    keys_were FW_LC_N, FW_LC_O, FW_LC_P, FW_LC_Q, FW_LC_R, FW_LC_S, FW_LC_T, FW_LC_U, FW_LC_V, FW_LC_W, FW_LC_X, FW_LC_Y, FW_LC_Z
    keys CH_SPACE, CH_A, CH_S, CH_D, CH_F, CH_G, CH_H, CH_J, CH_K, CH_L, CH_SPACE, CH_APOSTROPHE, CH_HYPHEN

.org 0x02100EA4
    keyboard_row 2, 4           ; was: ０-９ ． ， and an ideographic space
    keys_were FW_0, FW_1, FW_2, FW_3, FW_4, FW_5, FW_6, FW_7, FW_8, FW_9, FW_PERIOD, FW_COMMA, FW_SPACE
    keys CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_Z, CH_X, CH_C, CH_V, CH_B, CH_N, CH_M, CH_SPACE, CH_SPACE, CH_COMMA, CH_PERIOD

.close
```

</details>
